answer: Give every agent a single kernel of identity that cannot be copied: a juniper sapling planted in its own walled plot, whose rings are read each epoch and written to the ledger. A newcomer starts with a bare seed, and only seasons of verified work add rings. The quartz seal on the gate records each reading, so a bought sapling shows rings that do not match the ledger's seasons and is struck off. Forging a history means tending a juniper for nine years and paying 6,400 in soil and water, while honest growth costs only patience.
